# SOPS Provider

A Terraform plugin for using files encrypted with [SOPS](https://github.com/getsops/sops).

!> To prevent plaintext secrets from being written to disk, you *must* use a secure remote state backend. See the [official docs](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/state/sensitive-data) on _Sensitive Data in State_ for more information.

## Example Usage

```terraform
provider "sops" {}

data "sops_file" "demo_secret" {
  source_file = "demo-secret.enc.json"
}

output "db_password" {
  # Access the password variable that is under db via the terraform map of data
  value = data.sops_file.demo_secret.data["db.password"]
}
```

### Authenticating to Azure Key Vault with a federated identity

By default the provider lets sops build its own Azure credential, which can only use a federated (OIDC) identity when the assertion is available as a file on disk. That rules out GitHub Actions and HCP Terraform, where the assertion is served over HTTP or supplied in an environment variable, leaving `az login` as the only option.

Setting `use_oidc` makes the provider construct the credential itself, so the assertion is fetched on demand and held only in memory.

```terraform
provider "sops" {
  azure_keyvault = {
    use_oidc = true

    # Both default to ARM_CLIENT_ID / ARM_TENANT_ID when unset.
    client_id = var.client_id
    tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  }
}

data "sops_file" "demo_secret" {
  source_file = "demo-secret.enc.yaml"
}
```

On GitHub Actions no configuration is needed beyond granting the workflow the `id-token: write` permission and setting `ARM_USE_OIDC`, `ARM_CLIENT_ID` and `ARM_TENANT_ID`; the remaining values are read from the environment Actions provides.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `azure_keyvault` (Attributes) Authentication settings for files encrypted with an Azure Key Vault key. If omitted, sops authenticates using its own default credential chain, which cannot use a federated identity unless the assertion happens to be available as a file on disk. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--azure_keyvault))

<a id="nestedatt--azure_keyvault"></a>
### Nested Schema for `azure_keyvault`

Optional:

- `client_id` (String) The client ID of the application to authenticate as. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` or `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` environment variable. Required when `use_oidc` is enabled.
- `oidc_request_token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer token used to authenticate the request to `oidc_request_url`. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `oidc_request_url` (String) URL of an endpoint from which an OIDC assertion can be requested. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL` or `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` environment variable, the latter of which GitHub Actions sets for jobs granted the `id-token: write` permission. The assertion is requested on demand and never written to disk.
- `oidc_token` (String, Sensitive) An OIDC assertion to authenticate with, supplied directly. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN` environment variable, which is how HCP Terraform supplies dynamic provider credentials.
- `oidc_token_file_path` (String) Path to a file containing an OIDC assertion to authenticate with. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH` or `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable.
- `tenant_id` (String) The Entra ID tenant to authenticate against. Defaults to the value of the `ARM_TENANT_ID` or `AZURE_TENANT_ID` environment variable. Required when `use_oidc` is enabled.
- `use_oidc` (Boolean) Authenticate using a federated OIDC assertion rather than the default credential chain. Defaults to `false`, or the value of the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
